messages:
alex: Heads up — ran a focused perf sweep comparing FlashAttention-v2, paged-attn, and our fused-RoPE path under 4-bit quant. Seeing a surprising regression on seq_len >= 2048 when fused RoPE is enabled.

teju: Oof. Can you paste the micro-bench numbers? which quant backend (PACT/LSQ) and device?

alex: RTX A5000 (dedicated), pytorch 2.2, bitsandbytes 0.39 (LSQ-ish); runs:
```
# config: batch=1, seq=2048, kv_cache=true
flash-v2 + no-fused-rope: 840 toks/s
fused-rope + flash-v2: 620 toks/s  <-- regression
paged-attn + fused-rope: 760 toks/s
```

lina: Interesting that paged-attn + fused-rope recovers some of the perf. That suggests memory layout / TLB pressure rather than math correctness. Did you sample kernel occupancy / sm utilization?

alex: Attached a quick nvprof slice — occupancy drops ~20% on fused-rope+quant path, and there's a lot of memcpy between workspace buffers at high seq.

omar: Could be alignment when we pack quantized weights for fused RoPE. We use 128-byte alignment assumption for the non-quant path; quant changed packing to 32-byte to save mem and introduced extra re-align copy at launch.

teju: That matches a previous KV-cache regression we saw when introducing small-block quant packing. If the runtime kernel selection prefers fused-rope for model tags (rotary=true, alibi=false) we might be routing to a kernel that assumes a different workspace stride. Need a policy change: prefer paged-attn for seq>1024 when quantized weights are in small-block layout.

alex: Agreed. Quick checklist: (1) reproduce in CI microbench across seq: 512/1024/2048/4096, (2) capture per-kernel l2/stall stats, (3) test policy switch to prefer paged-attn for q4* variants.

bench-bot: Automated run results (last 5 mins):
```
model: llama-13b-rotary-q4_0
batch=1 seq=1024: flash-v2+fused-rope = 980 toks/s
batch=1 seq=2048: flash-v2+fused-rope = 615 toks/s
batch=1 seq=2048: paged-attn+fused-rope = 750 toks/s
batch=1 seq=4096: paged-attn+no-fused-rope = 430 toks/s
```

lina: Also validate KV cache behavior for long-running sessions. If fused-rope forces a workspace remap on first decode step with cached KV, that remap cost amortizes poorly for interactive workloads. We should capture cumulative latency over 1000 steps.

omar: I can instrument the KV flow to log `kv_copy_bytes` and `kv_remap_calls` per request id. If remap_calls > 0 for cached path, it's a bug unless we're upgrading packing format.

teju: One more thought — ALiBi handling differs: fused-RoPE path currently treats ALiBi as additive bias outside the kernel for quant flow; that adds an extra read pass. We should test fused-RoPE+ALiBi in both integrated and external-bias modes to see the I/O pattern.

alex: Plan: Omar to add KV remap logging + run microbench across seqs; Teju to prototype kernel-selection policy change and run canary on staging; Lina to collect nvprof traces and cumulative latencies for interactive pattern. We'll reconvene tomorrow at 11am PT. :thumbsup:

omar: On it — starting a bench sweep now, will post summarized CSV when done.

bench-bot: Note: created perf-issue #INF-827 to track quant+fused-rope long-seq regression and policy experiment.
